10.text: Alex's thesis is titled 'Long-Term Memory Systems for Small Language Models on Edge Devices'. It compares three retrieval strategies: Baseline (no retrieval), BM25 sparse retrieval, and dense vector retrieval using EmbeddingGemma 300M.

11.text: Alex uses an NVIDIA RTX 4050 6 GB laptop for all experiments. He runs Gemma 3 4B with 4-bit NF4 quantisation to stay within the VRAM budget.

12.text: Alex mentioned struggling with CUDA out-of-memory errors when loading Gemma 3 4B in full precision. Switching to 4-bit quantisation resolved the issue immediately.

13.text: Vector retrieval achieved the best answer relevance score of 4.39 out of 5.0 on LongMemEval, compared to 3.49 for the Baseline and 1.0 for BM25. BM25's score of 1.0 reflects that every response was scored at the minimum because the retrieved context misled the model.

14.text: BM25 retrieval had the highest retrieval latency at approximately 8,634 ms on LongMemEval, driven by query expansion via the SLM. Vector retrieval was far faster at 77 ms average.

15.text: Vector retrieval achieved a memory error rate of only 3.41 % on LongMemEval, versus 59.9 % for BM25 and 15.1 % for the Baseline.

16.text: On the LoCoMo benchmark (1,861 samples), vector retrieval achieved Recall@5 of 0.586 versus 0.571 for BM25 — a difference that was statistically non-significant (p = 0.61).

17.text: The statistical analysis used repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse-Geisser correction for violations of sphericity, followed by Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc paired t-tests. All five metrics showed significant main effects (p < 0.001).
